claim: Stale optimistic-concurrency token (version in request body) returns 409 Conflict

replacement: With the version in the body, a mismatch is `409 Conflict`; if you send it as an `If-Match` header instead, HTTP says `412 Precondition Failed`.

claim: 422 is named 'Unprocessable Entity'

replacement: `422 Unprocessable Content` (all four occurrences)

correction: Azure Circuit Breaker pattern: after failures reach a threshold, fail fast for a time-out, then half-open.

correction: Genie Spaces were renamed Genie Agents; still a managed text-to-SQL feature configured by domain experts.

claim: Stuffing 20+ tool schemas plus history into one context measurably degrades tool selection
correction: Directionally confirmed: vendor docs say tool selection accuracy degrades as the tool count grows (Claude: beyond 30-50 tools) and tool definitions bloat context. The 20+ figure is the candidate's own observed result, so left unchanged.

claim: MLflow tracing on every agent step / per-node tracing
correction: MLflow Tracing captures inputs, outputs and metadata of each intermediate step (LLM, tool, retrieval calls), with autologging for LangChain/LangGraph.

claim: Adversarial red-teaming using PyRIT
correction: PyRIT is an open-source framework for identifying risks in (red-teaming) generative AI systems.

claim: Attackers can craft rare-phrase queries to retrieve other tenants' documents from a shared vector collection with weak filters.
correction: Cross-tenant leakage via weak filters in shared vector stores is a named OWASP risk.

sources.title: OWASP LLM08:2025 Vector and Embedding Weaknesses

claim: Queries that inflate retrieval candidate sets and reranking are a denial-of-wallet/DoS vector.
correction: OWASP LLM10 Unbounded Consumption covers denial-of-wallet from resource-heavy queries.

claim: Kubernetes access is scoped by namespace RBAC, and read credentials are close to write scope.
correction: Kubernetes RBAC Roles/RoleBindings are namespace-scoped (ClusterRoles also exist); the 'one flag away from write' risk is the author's design note.

claim: LLMs can produce harmful output from benign prompts, so output guardrails are needed too.
correction: Harmful output can arise without a malicious prompt, so output-side handling/guardrails are needed.

claim: Validating an IdP token means checking signature, expiry and audience before authorization.
correction: OIDC requires issuer validation too; the current text already reads 'signature, issuer, expiry and audience' in both the full pack and Deep Dive (fixed in round 1).

RFC 8725: JSON Web Token Best Current Practices

claim: Token validation verifies the signature against the IdP's published keys (JWKS), expiry, and audience.
correction: Current text already includes 'the issuer' in the full pack and 'issuer' in the Deep Dive (fixed in round 1), matching OIDC Core 3.1.3.7.

sources.title: OpenID Connect Core 1.0, ID Token Validation (3.1.3.7)

claim: Regex filters cannot reliably detect unsafe SQL through aliases, nested selects, CTEs, comments or obfuscation; AST parsing is required.
correction: Regex cannot parse SQL grammar (CTEs, nesting, comments); parser/AST-based validation is the standard answer.

claim: Messaging systems route messages that exceed a bounded number of processing attempts to a dead-letter queue for inspection and replay.
correction: SQS moves a message to the DLQ after maxReceiveCount failed receives; other brokers have equivalents.

claim: With sampled tracing, only a subset of requests keep full traces, so a specific historical request may be unavailable.
correction: Head-sampled traces keep only a subset, so a given historical request may have no trace.

claim: Changing embedding model versions makes existing vectors incompatible and requires re-embedding.
correction: Vectors from different embedding models/versions live in different spaces, so a model change needs a re-embed.

claim: Google Drive permissions are per file and folder, inherited from folders, can include external sharing, and Drive offers change notifications.
correction: Drive permissions inherit from parent folders unless a folder has limited access turned on, which blocks inherited access (My Drive and shared drives); external sharing and change notifications are still accurate.
replacement: Per-file and folder sharing, inherited unless a folder has limited access; external sharing possible

claim: Annotating a LangGraph state list with operator.add makes parallel writes concatenate.
correction: Annotated[list, operator.add] sets a reducer so concurrent node updates concatenate.

claim: LLM tool/function calling has been a solved, mature capability for years.
correction: Function calling has been a standard API feature since June 2023 (over three years), but tool selection is not 'solved': function-calling benchmarks still show errors, especially multi-turn.
replacement: The mechanics of "LLM picks a tool" have been a standard model API feature since 2023. / Tool calling is a standard API feature; the tested question ...

sources.title: OpenAI: Function calling and other API updates (June 2023)

claim: Token streaming reduces perceived wait (earlier first output) but does not reduce total generation time or compute.
correction: Streaming moves the first token earlier; total generation work is unchanged.

claim: MLflow tracing can capture each LangGraph node and tool call.
correction: MLflow autologging for LangChain/LangGraph traces each node and tool call as spans.

claim: SharePoint permissions are granted via site and library groups, with item-level unique permissions breaking inheritance.
correction: SharePoint grants via site groups; libraries, folders and items can break inheritance for unique permissions.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn: Customize permissions for a SharePoint list or library

claim: Head sampling decides at trace start; tail sampling decides after completion, can keep slow/failed traces, and needs more infrastructure (buffering).
correction: OTel docs: tail sampling decides after the trace completes, can keep errors/slow traces, and needs a stateful collector tier.

claim: A client-side timeout on a write call does not establish whether the remote operation succeeded; the side effect may already have happened.
correction: A client timeout leaves the server outcome unknown; check status or use an idempotency key before retrying.

sources.title: AWS Builders' Library: Timeouts, retries and backoff with jitter

claim: Distributed queues cannot guarantee physical exactly-once execution; only effectively-once via idempotency.
correction: End-to-end exactly-once side effects are not achievable over at-least-once delivery; effectively-once needs idempotency/dedup.

claim: An API that returns 'accepted' (e.g. HTTP 202) has only queued the operation; completion must be tracked separately.
correction: RFC 9110: 202 means accepted for processing, which may not have completed.

claim: HTTP 429 with Retry-After signals rate limiting; 503 with Retry-After signals overload (L283).
correction: 429 for a full per-tenant/bounded admission queue is defensible (Google AIP maps RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED to 429); 503 + Retry-After for server overload (L283) is also RFC 9110-consistent. The pack uses both; not an error.

claim: Peak throttling surfaces as HTTP 429 from providers, mixed with the team's own gateway limits.
correction: Providers signal rate limits with HTTP 429.

claim: HTTP 409 Conflict fits a disallowed state transition and 422 Unprocessable Content fits typed validation failure.
correction: RFC 9110 defines 409 Conflict (conflict with current resource state) and 422 Unprocessable Content.

claim: A response-buffering proxy defeats token streaming.
correction: A buffering proxy holds the response and defeats streaming. The G18 'through every proxy' contradiction noted in round 1 is no longer present in G18.

claim: Idempotency keys prevent duplicate writes on retry; optimistic concurrency prevents lost updates.
correction: Idempotency keys dedupe retried writes; optimistic concurrency (version/ETag, If-Match) prevents lost updates.

sources.title: IETF draft: The Idempotency-Key HTTP Header Field

claim: An idempotency key makes a retried side-effecting API call return the original result rather than executing twice.
correction: With a provider that supports keys, a retry with the same key returns the first result; the text already notes legacy APIs may not.

sources.title: IETF draft: The Idempotency-Key HTTP Header Field

claim: Idempotency keys make a retried create return the original resource instead of a new one.
correction: Idempotency-key semantics return the original resource on retry.

sources.title: IETF draft: The Idempotency-Key HTTP Header Field

claim: Token streaming reduces perceived latency but not total generation time.
correction: Streaming improves perceived, not total, latency.

claim: Streaming output reduces perceived latency but not total latency or token cost.
correction: Streaming does not reduce total latency or token cost.

claim: Batch processing trades latency for throughput (and cost).
correction: Batch APIs trade latency (up to 24h window) for throughput and a discount.

claim: Streaming ASR APIs return interim/partial results during speech and a finalized segment at pauses/endpointing.
correction: Deepgram returns interim results then is_final/speech_final at endpointing.

claim: A client timeout does not tell you whether the server-side operation completed.
correction: Timeout outcome is ambiguous.

sources.title: AWS Builders' Library: Timeouts, retries and backoff with jitter

claim: Autoscaling has provisioning delay and does not raise external provider/API quotas.
correction: Autoscaling has provisioning lag and cannot raise third-party quotas.

claim: Partition skew means a few hot shards can dominate total batch completion time.
correction: Partition skew lets straggler shards set batch completion time.

claim: For parallel branches, elapsed latency is governed by the slowest branch plus overhead, not the sum; nested trace spans must not be double-counted.
correction: Parallel branches contribute the critical path, not the sum.

claim: Training runs on hundreds of GPUs over days will experience hardware failures.
correction: Meta reported 419 unexpected interruptions in 54 days on 16k GPUs for Llama 3 pretraining, mostly hardware.

sources.title: Llama 3 Herd of Models (Meta, 2024), section 3.3.4 reliability

claim: Output tokens are billed and generated sequentially, so longer outputs raise cost and completion latency.
correction: Output tokens are generated sequentially and billed (usually at a higher rate than input).

claim: Weight memory = params x bytes/param: 3B is 6/3/1.5 GB at 16/8/4-bit; 1B is 2/1/0.5 GB.
correction: Params x bytes/param gives 6/3/1.5 GB for 3B at 16/8/4-bit (decimal GB, ignoring quantisation scale overhead).

claim: P95 latency is the value at or below which 95% of measured requests complete; averages can hide slow tail requests.
correction: P95 is the 95th-percentile latency.

sources.title: Google SRE Book: Service Level Objectives

claim: Pretraining vs adapting a base model differs in compute budget by orders of magnitude.
correction: Pretraining vs adapting differs by orders of magnitude in compute.

claim: A queue smooths temporary bursts but cannot fix sustained overload: if arrival rate exceeds service rate the backlog grows without bound.
correction: If arrival rate exceeds service rate, backlog grows without bound; queues only absorb bursts.

claim: In a RAG pipeline, LLM generation calls dominate end-to-end latency.
correction: In typical RAG, LLM generation dominates end-to-end latency; context-dependent but standard.

claim: A 20-token vs a 2,000-token output differ in GPU work by ~100x.
correction: Current text already says 'decode work', which does differ ~100x (20 vs 2,000 decode steps); prefill is separate.

claim: Retries configured at multiple layers multiply total attempts (e.g. 3 x 3 x 3 = 27), amplifying load during outages.
correction: Retries at multiple layers multiply attempts (e.g. 3x3x3=27).

sources.title: Google SRE Book: Addressing Cascading Failures

claim: Cold starts slow the first request after idle; min replicas, warmers and keep-alive fix it at the cost of idle capacity.
correction: Cold starts slow first requests; min instances/provisioned capacity fix it at an idle cost.

claim: Uniform probabilistic sampling frequently retains zero traces of rare failures.
correction: Uniform sampling of rare events often keeps none.

claim: Call-recording consent requirements differ by region/jurisdiction.
correction: Recording consent rules vary by jurisdiction (one-party vs all-party in US states; GDPR lawful basis in the EU).

claim: Data-protection law (GDPR) purpose-limitation and minimisation principles apply to retained snapshots/results.
correction: GDPR Art. 5(1)(b) purpose limitation and 5(1)(c) data minimisation (and 5(1)(e) storage limitation) apply.

sources.title: GDPR Article 5, principles relating to processing

claim: Under ITIL, changes to configuration items go through the change-management (change control) process.
correction: Running changes through the customer's change process is standard ITIL practice (called 'change enablement' in ITIL 4); framed as the customer's own process, not a regulation.

claim: ASR/summary quality degrades on accented speech and different call types, hidden by averages.
correction: ASR error rates differ widely across speaker groups and accents; averages hide it.

sources.title: Koenecke et al. 2020, Racial disparities in automated speech recognition (PNAS)

claim: Bi-encoders embed query and document independently; cross-encoders jointly attend over both, making them more precise rerankers.
correction: Bi-encoders embed separately and compare by vector similarity; cross-encoders attend jointly and rerank more precisely.

claim: Using the lower bound of a bootstrapped confidence interval on the delta avoids shipping on noise.
correction: Gating on the lower bound of a bootstrapped CI is a standard way to avoid shipping on noise.

sources.title: Miller 2024 (Anthropic), Adding Error Bars to Evals

claim: A circuit breaker has three states: closed, open (after repeated failures), half-open (trial probe).
correction: Closed/open/half-open states are the standard pattern; half-open allows a trial call (some libraries allow a small number).

sources.title: Azure Architecture Center: Circuit Breaker pattern

claim: The circuit-breaker pattern opens after repeated failures, fails fast, then half-opens to probe recovery.
correction: Circuit breaker opens after failures, fails fast, then probes.

sources.title: Azure Architecture Center: Circuit Breaker pattern

claim: Constitutional AI uses AI feedback against a written set of principles to scale harmlessness labelling.
correction: Constitutional AI uses AI feedback against written principles (RLAIF) for harmlessness.

claim: LLM-generated conversation summaries can drop or distort information, affecting downstream task quality.
correction: Summaries can omit or distort facts.

claim: Static batching holds all sequences until the longest finishes; continuous (iteration-level) batching admits/evicts every decode step.
correction: Orca introduced iteration-level scheduling; static batches finish with their longest member.

claim: Repeated training tokens cost the same compute but give less learning signal.
correction: Duplicated tokens cost the same compute and add less signal; dedup improves models.

sources.title: Lee et al. 2021, Deduplicating Training Data Makes Language Models Better

claim: Dense embeddings poorly distinguish near-identical identifiers, while BM25 matches rare exact tokens reliably.
correction: Dense embeddings blur near-identical IDs; BM25 matches rare exact tokens.

claim: Distributed-trace sampling can omit the specific failing request.
correction: Sampling can drop the failing request's trace.

claim: Retries of transient failures should use bounded attempts with exponential backoff plus jitter to avoid synchronized retry storms.
correction: Bounded retries with exponential backoff and jitter avoid retry storms.

sources.title: AWS Builders' Library: Timeouts, retries and backoff with jitter

claim: Groundedness/faithfulness metrics measure support by retrieved context, not factual correctness or currency.
correction: Groundedness measures support by context, not truth or currency.

claim: Dense vector search captures semantic similarity while lexical/keyword search handles exact identifiers; hybrid search combines both.
correction: Hybrid search combines dense and lexical signals.

claim: HyDE generates a hypothetical answer, embeds it and uses it as the retrieval query without showing it to the user.
correction: HyDE embeds a generated hypothetical document as the query; it is not shown to the user.

sources.title: Gao et al. 2022, Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels (HyDE)

claim: Most interview candidates fumble the question of how they know their AI system is working.
correction: The 'most candidates fumble' claim is already attributed to the source question bank (purchased material, not committed and not checkable here); no population data exists to verify it, and the attribution is the right hedge.

claim: KV-cache memory limits concurrent sequences per GPU; when full, requests queue.
correction: Current text already says 'forces queueing or preemption' (fixed in round 1), matching vLLM's preemption behaviour.

claim: Little's Law: items in system = arrival rate x time in system.
correction: Little's Law L = λW, i.e. concurrency = throughput x latency.

sources.title: Little 1961, A Proof for the Queuing Formula L = λW

claim: Autoregressive generation is memory-bandwidth-bound and runs well below peak FLOP throughput.
correction: Decode at small batch is memory-bandwidth-bound and runs well below peak FLOPs.

claim: LLM output variance means small-sample comparisons are statistically unreliable.
correction: LLM output variance makes small-sample comparisons unreliable.

sources.title: Miller 2024 (Anthropic), Adding Error Bars to Evals

claim: Prefill processes input in parallel and governs TTFT (scales with input tokens); decode is sequential and governs tokens/sec (scales with output tokens).
correction: Prefill is parallel and sets TTFT; decode is sequential.

claim: Prefill processes the prompt in parallel and determines TTFT; decode is sequential per token and determines total time.
correction: Same as C341.

claim: Prefill (parallel over the prompt) sets TTFT; decode (one token per step) sets per-token speed.
correction: Same as C341.

claim: Streaming improves perceived latency but not total latency.
correction: Streaming changes perceived, not total, latency.

claim: LLM graders drift when their rubric or underlying model changes.
correction: LLM judges drift with rubric or judge-model changes.

claim: LoRA trains small added low-rank weights with the base frozen; QLoRA applies LoRA to a 4-bit quantised base.
correction: LoRA trains low-rank adapters on a frozen base; QLoRA does so on a 4-bit (NF4) quantised base.

claim: There is no universally optimal chunk size for RAG; the best size depends on documents and queries.
correction: No universally optimal chunk size.

sources.title: Pinecone: Chunking strategies for LLM applications

claim: RAG-Fusion is multi-query retrieval combined with Reciprocal Rank Fusion.
correction: RAG-Fusion = multiple generated queries fused with RRF.

sources.title: Cormack, Clarke & Buettcher 2009, Reciprocal Rank Fusion

claim: Rejection sampling (in LLM data generation) = generate many solutions and keep only verified ones.
correction: Rejection sampling in LLM data generation keeps only samples that pass a check (as in STaR/RFT).

claim: Rerankers only reorder the candidate set, so they cannot fix recall failures in first-stage retrieval.
correction: Rerankers reorder candidates only; they cannot recover missed documents.

claim: Without a KL/drift penalty, RL policies reward-hack the scorer.
correction: Optimising against a proxy scorer without a KL/drift penalty exploits its blind spots (reward overoptimisation); 'will' is strong but well supported.

sources.title: Gao, Schulman & Hilton 2022, Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization

claim: RLHF fits a reward model from human comparisons and optimises the policy against it with a KL penalty to the reference.
correction: InstructGPT: reward model from human comparisons, PPO with a per-token KL penalty to the SFT model.

claim: Vector/semantic search returns similar items and cannot compute counts, recency or field changes.
correction: Pure vector search returns similar items; counts, recency and field comparisons need structured queries.

claim: Semantic search finds similar items but cannot count, find the most recent, or sum a field.
correction: Same as C355.

claim: Speculative decoding reduces inference latency and is supported by some serving stacks.
correction: Speculative decoding cuts latency and is supported in vLLM, TensorRT-LLM and others.

claim: SLI = measured indicator, SLO = target for it, SLA = customer agreement typically with consequences (e.g. credits) when missed.
correction: SLI/SLO/SLA definitions as in the Google SRE book; SLAs carry consequences.

sources.title: Google SRE Book: Service Level Objectives

claim: Tensor parallelism splits matrices within a node and needs fast intra-node interconnect; pipeline parallelism has bubble overhead.
correction: Tensor parallelism splits matrices within a node over fast links (NVLink); pipeline parallelism has bubbles.

claim: Explicit user feedback (thumbs up/down) is sparse and biased and can disagree with actual task outcomes.
correction: Explicit ratings are sparse and biased.

claim: A workflow that calls an LLM along predefined steps is distinct from an agent that dynamically chooses its own steps/tools.
correction: Anthropic distinguishes workflows (predefined code paths) from agents (model directs its own process).

claim: ZeRO/FSDP shard weights, gradients and optimizer state so per-GPU memory falls with GPU count.
correction: ZeRO-3/FSDP shard params, grads and optimiser state, so per-GPU model-state memory falls with GPU count.

claim: Google Drive permissions are per file and folder, inherited from folders, can include external sharing, and Drive offers change notifications.
correction: Inheritance still holds by default, but a folder with limited access turned on blocks inherited access (My Drive and shared drives), so 'inherited' needs the exception. Fixed in the full pack, Main and Deep Dive.
replacement: Full pack: 'Per-file and folder sharing, inherited unless a folder has limited access; external sharing possible'. Main: 'Inherited sharing (limited-access folders can block it), ...'. Deep Dive: 'inherited permissions (a limited-access folder blocks inheritance), ...'.
